tax_burden.notes: Combined corporate rate of about 30 percent covers the 15 percent federal corporate income tax, the 5.5 percent solidarity surcharge on it (15.825 percent together), and the municipal trade tax that runs roughly 14 to 17 percent depending on the local multiplier (30 percent in Berlin, near 33 percent in Munich). Personal dividends and share gains are taxed at a flat 26.375 percent (25 percent plus solidarity surcharge). VAT of 19 percent is paid by the customer and is excluded from the headline total.

_meta.source: PwC Worldwide Tax Summaries Germany corporate (CIT 15% + 5.5% soli = 15.825%, trade tax 3.5% x municipal multiplier, combined ~30-33%); PwC/DLA Piper individual (dividends and private share gains 26.375%); GTAI/TK employer social insurance ~20-21% of gross; Tax Foundation/PwC VAT 19%. total_pct is the locked blend.
_meta.method: corporation_tax_pct = combined federal CIT + solidarity surcharge + typical municipal trade tax (Berlin-level ~30%, range 30-33% across cities). dividend_tax_pct and capital_gains_pct = top flat investor rate incl. solidarity surcharge (church tax excluded). business_rates_pct_equiv modeled at ~1.0% profit-equivalent (recurring real-property tax Grundsteuer is minor; the larger premises levy, trade tax, is already inside corporation_tax_pct). employer_oncost_pct = employer share of statutory social insurance as % of gross wage. total_pct = corp + (1 - corp/100)*dividend + business_rates_pct_equiv = 30 + 0.70*26.375 + 1.0 = 49.46, rounded.

_meta.source: World Bank Doing Business 2020 EoDB score 79.7 (rank 24); WGI government effectiveness 1.55, political stability 0.12; domestic credit to private sector ~75% GDP; VC 2024 ~4.1B USD; GDP/cap PPP 73552, growth 0.8%, labour force 43M; price level above OECD avg
_meta.method: ease_of_business 7: EoDB 79.7 with strong contract enforcement, bureaucracy slows starts. talent_pool 8: 43M labour force, top vocational and engineering depth. access_to_financing 6: bank-led system, modest credit/GDP ~75% and small VC ~4.1B relative to size. political_stability 8: high government effectiveness 1.55 and stable coalition governance. economic_reward 7: high GDP/cap PPP 73552 and large market, dragged by 0.8% growth. affordability 4: above-OECD price level makes operating expensive.

banking.notes: A foreigner can open a business account, and a limited company must to deposit its capital. Traditional banks usually require in-person identity checks and may hesitate with non-resident directors. Digital providers open fully online with a German IBAN and English support, though the capital-deposit formation account often needs a full-licence bank.

_meta.method: Each fee, the VAT line and structures confirmed across 2+ independent sources; money converted at fx_to_usd 1.146815.

notes.hire: Skilled labour is available but tight in tech and engineering, with notice periods slowing the start date of senior hires.
notes.contract: Open-ended contracts are the default and works council and collective agreement rules shape terms.
notes.fire: Dismissal protection is strong once past the probation window, often needing a valid reason, long notice and negotiated settlements.
notes.recruiting: Deep pools in engineering, manufacturing and professional services, thinner in some software niches.

_meta.source: Pay loaded from Destatis 2024 average full-time gross of roughly 50,000 to 56,000 EUR plus ~21% employer social insurance, converted at fx 1.146815. Languages from German home-language shares (German dominant, small recognized Sorbian minority). Labour law from German dismissal protection and notice rules.
_meta.method: Representative white-collar base by level times 1.21 fully-loaded employer multiplier times fx to USD; talent_depth scored on engineering and professional output; hire/fire from dismissal protection and notice regime.

_meta.source: Median equivalised disposable income Germany 25000 euro (Eurostat, 2022) held; average from national-accounts household net disposable income per capita ~28500 euro modeled; OECD Income Distribution Database disposable Gini 0.309 (2022) held; top-decile and top-percentile disposable incomes modeled. Household consumption structure Destatis 2023 (euro/month per household): housing/energy/maintenance 37.5, food/beverages/tobacco 14.4, transport 11.9, recreation/sport/culture 8.6, restaurants and hotels 6.8, clothing 3.7 plus furnishings 4.5, remainder (health, communication, education, insurance, misc) ~12.6.
_meta.method: Median held (25000 euro *1.146815=28670; median reference year 2022). Average modeled from NA per-capita net disposable income (28514 euro *1.146815=32700). Top10/top1 modeled. Gini held from OECD IDD. Spend mapped from Destatis EVS/national-accounts consumption structure into seven buckets: housing/energy/maintenance to housing_utilities (broader than COICOP-04 as it bundles maintenance), transport, food to food_drink, recreation/culture to recreation, restaurants and hotels to dining_out, clothing plus furnishings to household_goods, remainder to other; sums to 100.

_raw.income_basis: Annual disposable income per capita, nominal USD, converted from euro at fx 1.146815. Average = national-accounts household net disposable income per person. Median = equivalised household disposable income per person (post-tax-and-transfer). Top10 and top1 = modeled mean disposable income of the top decile and top percentile per capita.

_meta.source: Energy: business retail EUR 0.238/kWh = USD 0.276 (Sept 2025 GlobalPetrolPrices); non-household medium consumers EUR 0.2264/kWh H2 2025 (Eurostat) = ~USD 0.260. Held range; set USD 0.27. Rent: prime EUR 45-59/sqm/month in top cities (Munich 55-59, Frankfurt 52-54, Berlin 45) but Munich weighted average EUR 26.90 and rest-of-market EUR 20.25/sqm/month (Colliers, Cushman & Wakefield, CBRE Q3 2025). Representative secondary/multi-city EUR 24/sqm/month x12 = EUR 288/sqm/yr x 1.146815 = USD 330. Labour: average gross annual wage EUR 50257 in 2024 (Statista/Destatis), OECD avg wage ~EUR 60k area; x 1.20 employer social contributions (~20%) = ~EUR 60300 x 1.146815 = USD 69150. Setup: GmbH notary EUR 350-850 + commercial register ~EUR 150 + Gewerbeanmeldung EUR 15-65, all-in ~EUR 1000 (excludes EUR 25000 share capital) x 1.146815 = USD 1150.
_meta.method: Money converted with fx_to_usd 1.146815. Energy triangulated from 2 sources (EUR 0.226-0.238/kWh -> USD 0.26-0.276, set USD 0.27). Rent from monthly EUR/sqm x12 then x fx (modeled secondary/weighted-average basis, below trophy prime). Labour = gross wage x (1 + employer social ~0.20) x fx. Setup = sum of statutory GmbH formation fees x fx, share capital excluded.

_meta.source: Energy: industrial electricity about 23 c/kWh, roughly 25% above the EU average, among the highest in Europe (Eurostat H2-2024; cross-source). Skills: chronic skilled-labour shortage and ageing workforce widely documented. Exit: very large succession pipeline (about 600k SMEs seeking successors by 2028; about 224k handovers planned through 2024), a functioning intermediary market with search funds and PE; supply-heavy and buyer-favourable. Multiples: small-business deals commonly 3x-5x EBITDA with a small-company discount, set here on an owner-earnings/SDE basis. Demand: near-stagnant 0.8% real growth, industrial softness. Currency: EUR reserve currency, low volatility.
_meta.method: Held on energy and skills (2+ credible sources agree) and on the succession/exit market structure; risk scores normalized across the peer set; multiples narrowed to small-business SDE range.
